settings.name: Ironvale Suspension Works
settings.tagline: Suspension made in Dutton Falls since 1988.
settings.legal: Ironvale Suspension Works LLC. Arden, Halcyon, Kestrel and Voss are fictional vehicle makes.
settings.warrantyText: Every part is covered against defects in materials and workmanship for the period on its product page, from the date of purchase, for the original buyer. Keep your receipt and the serial tag. Start a claim on the Contact page.
settings.quoteText: The fitment desk answers quote requests within one business day, by email, with freight to your door or to your dealer.
settings.certifications:
IATF 16949 quality management
ISO 14001 environmental management
DOT-compliant brake line brackets
Salt spray tested 1,000 hours
100 percent dyno tested dampers
settings.shipFrom: Ships from Dutton Falls, Ohio. In-stock orders placed before 2 p.m. Eastern leave the same day.

products.name: Apex Coilovers · Arden Meridian (Gen 1)
products.summary: Height and damping adjustable coilovers for the Arden Meridian.
products.text:
Apex coilovers give the Arden Meridian adjustable ride height and damping in one bolt-in kit. Each damper is built and dyno tested in Dutton Falls, then matched to a spring rate chosen for the weight and geometry of this sedan.

Set the height with the threaded lower mounts, then dial the damping to suit the road, the tires and the day. The adjusters are reachable with the wheels on.
products.torque: Top nut 44 ft·lb, lower mount bolt 85 ft·lb, wheel nuts to the vehicle manual.

products.name: Apex Strut Assemblies · Arden Meridian
products.summary: Assembled front strut pair for the Arden Meridian, OE ride height.
products.text:
Complete strut assemblies for the Arden Meridian: damper, spring, mount, bearing plate and bump stop, assembled and torqued at the factory. No spring compressor, no guesswork.

The valving restores the ride the car left the showroom with, and the springs hold the stock height to the millimeter.
features: Bump stop and dust boot included

specs.name: Mount
specs.value: Complete with bearing plate and bump stop

products.torque: Top mount nuts 25 ft·lb, knuckle bolts 125 ft·lb.

products.name: Apex Shocks · Arden Meridian
products.summary: Monotube apex series shocks for the Arden Meridian.
products.text:
Apex shocks for the Arden Meridian replace the worn dampers with a monotube design tuned for this sedan. The valving smooths broken pavement without going soft in corners.

Mounts, bushings and hardware are included, and every shock is gas charged and checked on the dyno before it is boxed.
products.torque: Upper mount 30 ft·lb, lower mount 65 ft·lb.

products.name: Apex Control Arms · Arden Meridian
products.summary: Forged front control arms for the Arden Meridian.
products.text:
Forged control arms for the Arden Meridian. The aluminum arms save unsprung weight and add camber adjustment for an aligned, planted front end.

Ball joints are sealed and greaseable, and the bushings are pressed before shipping so the arms bolt straight on.
box: Two control arms with ball joints
products.torque: Pivot bolts 90 ft·lb at ride height, ball joint nut 55 ft·lb plus cotter pin.

products.name: Apex Bushing Kit · Arden Meridian
products.summary: Full polyurethane bushing kit for the Arden Meridian.
products.text:
A full polyurethane bushing kit for the Arden Meridian: control arms, sway bar and subframe mounts in one box. Polyurethane stops the deflection that makes an older sedan feel vague, and it never dries out and cracks.

Each bushing is molded with a graphite-impregnated compound, so it stays quiet without constant greasing.
features: Will not dry out or crack
products.torque: Tighten all pivot bolts at ride height to the vehicle manual.

products.text:

Springs ship as a matched pair with pressed bushings, and every leaf is shot peened and powder coated.

posts.title: Second generation Circuit coilovers go on sale
posts.summary: The Circuit line gets inverted front dampers, a lighter spring perch and the same 32-way adjustment.
posts.body:
Two years of track days went into the second generation of our Circuit coilovers. The front dampers are now inverted, which stiffens the strut against side loads and keeps the piston moving freely under hard cornering. The spring perch loses almost a pound per corner.

Adjustment stays at 32 clicks of rebound and compression, and every kit still leaves the dyno with a printed curve in the box. The first applications are the Arden Vale and the Kestrel Falcon, with the Arden Meridian following in the spring.

Existing Circuit owners can send their kits in for a rebuild with the new pistons; ask your dealer or use the quote form.

posts.title: Plant open house: see the forge and the test lab
posts.summary: Saturday, November 7. Tours every half hour, from the billet rack to the shipping dock.
posts.body:
Once a year we open the doors in Dutton Falls. Walk the forge line, watch a control arm come out of the die, and stand next to the shock dyno while it runs a full temperature sweep. Engineers from every team will be on the floor to answer questions.

Tours start at 9 a.m. and run every half hour until 2 p.m. Closed-toe shoes are required, and safety glasses are provided at the door. Bring the family; the coffee is on us.

posts.title: Three days, one booth and a lot of questions about air ride
posts.summary: What we heard at the fall aftermarket show, and what it means for next year's catalog.
posts.body:
The booth was busy from the first bell to the last. The most common question, by a wide margin, was about air suspension for half-ton trucks that tow on the weekend and commute during the week. The second was whether the Trail shocks fit the new Voss Terra. They do, from the 2018 model year.

We also showed the leveling kit prototype for the Halcyon Caldera and took more than two hundred dealer leads. If you spoke with us and have not heard back yet, you will this week.

posts.title: Why we forge control arms instead of casting them
posts.summary: Grain flow, fatigue life and the simple fact that a forged arm bends before it breaks.
posts.body:
A cast arm is cheaper to make. A forged arm is better to drive on. When steel or aluminum is forged, the grain follows the shape of the part, so the arm is strongest exactly where the loads run. In a casting, the grain is random and the part can carry a hidden void.

Our arms are forged in two blows on a 1,600-ton press, trimmed, heat treated and then machined for the ball joint and bushing bores. Every lot is cut, polished and inspected under the microscope. In a worst case overload, a forged arm bends and the driver feels it; it does not snap.

posts.title: 1,000 hours in the salt spray cabinet
posts.summary: How we test coatings, and why the hardware matters as much as the body.
posts.body:
Our coatings have to survive northern winters, so every finish spends 1,000 hours in a salt spray cabinet before it goes into production. The damper bodies are hard anodized, the collars and hardware are zinc-nickel plated, and the springs are powder coated over a zinc phosphate base.

The most common failure in aftermarket suspension is not the damper; it is a seized adjuster collar after two winters. That is why the collars get the same coating as the hardware, and why we ship anti-seize in every coilover box.

posts.title: Leveling kit for the Halcyon Caldera ships this month
posts.summary: Two inches up front, factory ride, and room for a 33-inch tire.
posts.body:
The Trail leveling kit for the Halcyon Caldera is in stock. It lifts the front two inches with machined strut spacers and adds a one-inch rear block, so the truck sits level with an empty bed and keeps the factory ride.

With the kit fitted, a 33-inch tire clears at full lock. Installation takes about four hours with hand tools; an alignment is required afterward.

posts.title: Second apprenticeship class starts in January
posts.summary: Twelve paid places in machining, assembly and quality, in partnership with the county technical college.
posts.body:
Our first apprenticeship class graduated in August, and nine of the twelve stayed on. The second class starts in January with places in CNC machining, shock assembly and quality inspection. Apprentices are paid from day one and split their week between the plant floor and the technical college.

Applications are open on the Careers page until December 1.

posts.title: A fleet program for upfitters and municipalities
posts.summary: Volume pricing, consolidated shipping and a dedicated line for fleet managers.
posts.body:
Fleet managers asked for three things: one price list, one shipment a week and one person to call. The new fleet program gives them all three. Haul shocks, leaf springs and air systems for vans and pickups are stocked in fleet quantities, and orders placed by Thursday ship together on Monday.

Use the quote form and choose Fleet in the company field to be routed to the fleet desk.

posts.title: Spring rate, explained without the math
posts.summary: What a number like 450 lb/in means for how a car feels, and how to pick one.
posts.body:
A spring rate of 450 lb/in means the spring compresses one inch for every 450 pounds pressed on it. Double the rate and the car moves half as much over the same bump; it also leans half as much in a corner. Higher is not better. The right rate depends on the weight on that corner, the motion ratio of the suspension and what the car is for.

Our street kits run a little above stock, so the car stays flat without crashing over expansion joints. Track kits go higher and pair the springs with dampers that can control them. If you are unsure, ask: the fitment team answers rate questions every day.

posts.title: Fourteen new dealers in the West
posts.summary: From Arizona to Washington, more shops now stock the line and install it.
posts.body:
The western dealer network grew by fourteen shops this quarter. Nine are installers with alignment racks, three are retail stores and two are distributors who supply smaller garages in their regions.

Find them on the Dealers page. If your shop would like to carry the brand, the dealer inquiry form is there too.

posts.title: Every damper, on the dyno, every time
posts.summary: Why we test 100 percent instead of sampling, and what we look for in the curve.
posts.body:
Most factories dyno a sample from each batch. We dyno every damper. The test takes ninety seconds: a sweep of velocities in compression and rebound, at room temperature and again warm. The software compares the curve to the master and flags anything outside two percent.

It costs us a little time per unit and it means a damper that leaves the building does exactly what the one next to it does. The printout is in the box.

posts.title: Warehouse expansion adds 40,000 square feet
posts.summary: More stock on the shelf, faster shipping and a second dock for carriers.
posts.body: The warehouse expansion is finished. The new building adds 40,000 square feet of racking, a second loading dock and a packing line sized for air suspension systems, which ship in large boxes. Most in-stock orders now leave the same day when placed before 2 p.m. Eastern.

posts.title: Holiday shipping schedule
posts.summary: Carrier cut-off times for the last two weeks of December.
posts.body: Orders placed before noon Eastern on December 22 ship the same day. The plant closes December 24 to 26 and December 31 to January 1. Built-to-order systems placed after December 15 ship in the first week of January.

jobs.title: CNC Machinist, second shift
jobs.shift: 2nd shift, Mon to Thu, 3:30 p.m. to 2 a.m.
jobs.summary: Run and set up 4-axis mills machining forged control arms and damper bodies.
jobs.body:
You will set up and run 4-axis horizontal mills that machine forged aluminum and steel suspension parts. Setups change two or three times a shift, so you will read drawings, touch off tools, prove out programs and hold tolerances to a thousandth.

What you bring

  • Three years on CNC mills, with setup experience
  • Comfortable with calipers, micrometers and bore gauges
  • A steady hand with offsets and a habit of checking the first part

What we offer

  • Four 10-hour days with a 10 percent shift premium
  • Health, dental and vision from day 60
  • Tool allowance and paid training on our controls

blocks.title: Suspension built to be driven on.
blocks.text: Coilovers, struts, shocks, arms and lift kits, forged, machined and dyno tested under one roof in {town}. Find what fits your vehicle, request a quote or visit a dealer near you.

blocks.title: Everything between the frame and the road
blocks.text: Nine families, one standard. Every part is designed for a specific vehicle and tested as a set.

blocks.title: Thirty-eight years in the same town
blocks.text:
{name} started in a two-bay machine shop on Foundry Road in 1988, making replacement springs for local farm trucks. Today the plant covers twelve acres, employs 180 people and ships to dealers in 36 states.

We still answer the phone ourselves.
blocks.label: Our story

blocks.title: Owner of a Kestrel Falcon, via a dealer survey
blocks.text: They told me the rear bar would not clear my spare. It cleared. Then they called two weeks later to ask how the car felt.

blocks.title: Not sure what fits? Ask.
blocks.text: Send the year, make and model and we will come back with the right kit and a price within one business day.
blocks.label: Request a quote

blocks.title: From billet to boxed kit, under one roof
blocks.text: Forging, machining, heat treatment, coating, assembly and testing happen on the same twelve acres. Nothing leaves the site between the raw bar and the finished part.
blocks.label: Request a quote

items.title: Forging
items.text: Two hot forging lines, 600 and 1,600 tons, for aluminum and steel arms, brackets and spring seats.

items.title: CNC machining
items.text: Horizontal and vertical mills, turning centers and a dedicated cell for damper bodies and threaded collars.

items.title: Heat treatment
items.text: In-house solution treatment and aging for aluminum, quench and temper for steel, with lot traceability.

items.title: Coating
items.text: Hard anodizing, zinc-nickel plating and a powder coating line with zinc phosphate pre-treatment.

items.title: Assembly
items.text: Damper assembly in a clean room, spring and strut assembly on torque-controlled benches.

items.title: Testing
items.text: Shock dyno, four-post rig, fatigue frames and a salt spray cabinet, plus a development fleet of twelve vehicles.

blocks.title: Tested before you see it
blocks.text:
Every new application goes through the same gate: dyno curves against the target, 500,000 cycles on the fatigue frame, a four-post sweep for ride, then two weeks on the road with the development fleet. Only then is the valving signed off and the part released.

The same lab checks production. Every damper gets a dyno sweep and every coating lot gets a salt spray coupon.
blocks.label: Read the tech notes

blocks.title: Certifications and standards
blocks.text: Our quality system is audited every year, and every lot of forgings is traceable to the heat number of the bar it came from.

items.title: Tell us the vehicle
items.text: Year, make, model, how it is used and what you want it to do differently.

items.title: We measure
items.text: A development car comes to the plant, or we work from your drawings and corner weights.

items.title: Prototype and test
items.text: First parts in four to six weeks, then dyno, rig and road testing with you.

items.title: Production
items.text: Tooling is made, first articles are approved and the application joins the catalog or stays private to you.

blocks.title: Four markets, one plant
blocks.text: Aftermarket, OEM and tier supply, fleet and motorsport. Each one has its own team at the fitment desk and its own part of the catalog.

items.title: Aftermarket
items.text: Dealers and installers in 36 states carry the Apex, Circuit and Trail lines. Catalog, counter displays and training are part of the program.
items.label: Find a dealer

items.title: OEM and tier supply
items.text: Forged arms, spring seats and complete strut assemblies for low and mid volume vehicle programs, with PPAP documentation.
items.label: Start a conversation

items.title: Fleet and upfitters
items.text: Haul shocks, leaf springs and air systems for vans and pickups, in fleet quantities, on a weekly consolidated shipment.
items.label: Ask about fleet pricing

items.title: Motorsport
items.text: Circuit coilovers, spherical arms and adjustable bars for club racing and time attack, with trackside rebuild support.
items.label: See the Circuit line

blocks.title: A county fleet that stopped replacing shocks every year
blocks.text:
A county road department ran forty pickups on gravel. Stock shocks lasted a season. After switching to Haul shocks with the heavy duty leaf packs, the fleet went three years without a damper change and cut its spring replacements by half.

The program now ships one consolidated pallet a month, with a single invoice.
blocks.label: Ask about fleet pricing

blocks.title: A regional time attack champion on Circuit coilovers
blocks.text: A privateer team came to the plant with a Kestrel Falcon and a lap time to beat. Two days of four-post work and a week of track testing produced a valving that took 0.8 seconds off their best. The same setup is now the catalog Circuit kit for the Falcon.
blocks.label: See the Circuit line

items.title: Do you sell direct?
items.text: Drivers buy through our dealers or request a quote here; fleets and OEM programs work directly with the plant.

items.title: What is the minimum order for a private label part?
items.text: It depends on the tooling. Most programs start at 500 pieces a year.

items.title: Can you supply PPAP documentation?
items.text: Yes. Level 3 PPAP packages are standard for tier supply programs.

items.title: Where do you ship from?
items.text: Everything ships from Dutton Falls, Ohio, by parcel or LTL freight.

blocks.title: Tell us about your program
blocks.text: The industry desks answer within one business day.
blocks.label: Request a quote

blocks.title: Find a dealer or installer
blocks.text: Our dealers stock the catalog, install it and align it. Pick a state on the map or filter the list below.

blocks.title: Dealers and installers
blocks.text: Premier dealers keep the full catalog in stock and have installers trained at the plant.

blocks.title: Carry the line
blocks.text: Independent shops, distributors and online stores with an installation partner are welcome. Tell us about your shop and the dealer team will call.

blocks.title: From the plant floor
blocks.text: Product launches, tech notes, trade shows and what is happening in Dutton Falls.

blocks.title: Make things that matter
blocks.text: 180 people forge, machine, assemble and test suspension in {town}. We hire for skill and train for the rest, with paid apprenticeships every January.
blocks.label: See open positions

items.title: Health from day 60
items.text: Medical, dental and vision for you and your family, with most of the premium paid by the company.

items.title: Paid training
items.text: Controls, metrology, forklift, first aid. Apprentices get college tuition paid in full.

items.title: Four-day weeks on second shift
items.text: Four 10-hour days with a 10 percent premium, and a three-day weekend every week.

items.title: Profit sharing
items.text: A share of the year's profit, paid in December, to everyone on site.

blocks.title: Open positions
blocks.text: Apply online with a résumé. We answer every application within two weeks.

items.title: I have no manufacturing experience. Can I apply?
items.text: Yes. Warehouse and apprentice roles need no experience, and we train on the job.

items.title: Do you sponsor visas?
items.text: Not at this time.

items.title: What is the interview like?
items.text: A phone call, then a visit to the plant where you meet the team and, for floor roles, try the work for an hour.

blocks.title: A machine shop that grew up
blocks.text: {name} started in 1988 in a two-bay shop on Foundry Road, making replacement springs for local farm trucks. The shop is still there, and so is the habit of making things properly.

blocks.title: From farm trucks to forgings
blocks.text:
Ruth Ironvale and her father opened the shop with one lathe, one press brake and a contract to rebuild leaf springs for the county. Within five years the springs had a name, and customers were asking for shocks to go with them.

The first forging press arrived in 1996, the test lab in 2004 and the second plant building in 2019. The company is still family owned and still makes every part in {town}.

The second plant building doubles machining capacity.

Cast a part we could forge
Ship a kit without its guide and torque sheet
Sell a kit for a car we have not tested on
